newsitem.title: UK: UK investment in Romania should swell -ambassador.
newsitem.headline: UK investment in Romania should swell -ambassador.

text.p: British investment of as much as $1 billion in Romania in the next three years is a realistic target, Romania's newly appointed ambassador to Britain, Radu Onofrei, said on Thursday.
"Britain could have a much stronger presence in central and eastern Europe," Onofrei told Reuters at an Embassy reception.

"British foreign investment in the past seven years reached $133 million which is below the levels of some other foreign investors like Germany, France and South Korea, so we hope that British companies will be more active. Realistically we should reach $1 billion in the next three years."
During Onofrei's term of office he would also like to intensify the two countries' political dialogue, "especially at this crucial moment with the extension of NATO", he said.
He added Romania's integration in the European Union was a "definitive option" for the country.
Onofrei, whose previous posting was in Cairo, said he had discussed with Queen Elizabeth earlier in the day Romania's desire to see Britain play a bigger part.
"I had a chance to talk to Her Majesty about the British-Romanian relationship and she is positive in encouraging the development of this," he said.
"We see Britain as the main bridge between us and the United States. Britain also has skills and experience in dealing with the Middle East and South east Asia," he said.
